marks.gloss_en: ״למענך״ מבעי ליה, אלא למען אברהם שקראך אדון -- the verse should have said 'for Your sake'; 'for the sake of the Lord' therefore means for the sake of Abraham, who called You Lord

Rav: even Daniel was answered only on account of Abraham -- 'and now hear, our God, the prayer of Your servant... and cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary, for the sake of the Lord' (Dan 9:17)
from the day the Holy One created the world no one called Him 'Lord' until Abraham came and called Him Lord -- 'and he said, my Lord God, by what shall I know that I will inherit it' (Gen 15:8)
Rav's reading of the verse's 'for the sake of the Lord': for the sake of Abraham, who called You Lord
one does not placate a person in the hour of his anger -- 'My face will go, and I will give you rest' (Ex 33:14)
whoever fixes a place for his prayer, his enemies fall beneath him
Rav Huna set the verses against each other: it is written 'to afflict them' (II Sam 7:10) and it is written 'to destroy them' (I Chr 17:9)
at first -- to afflict them; and in the end -- to destroy them
from the day the Holy One created His world no one gave thanks to Him until Leah came and thanked Him -- 'this time I will give thanks to the Lord' (Gen 29:35)
שנאמר: עזבי תורה יהללו רשע ושמרי תורה יתגרו בם (Prov 28:4)
one is permitted to provoke the wicked in this world
תניא נמי הכי, רבי דוסתאי ברבי מתון אומר: מותר להתגרות ברשעים בעולם הזה, שנאמר עזבי תורה יהללו רשע וגו' -- the baraita restates the permission in R' Dostai's name (his own commit at 7b.16)
ואם לחשך אדם לומר: והא כתיב אל תתחר במרעים אל תקנא בעשי עולה -- the verse tells one NOT to contend with evil-doers
אמור לו: מי שלבו נוקפו אומר כן -- only one whose own conscience strikes him reads the verse so
אלא: אל תתחר במרעים -- להיות כמרעים, אל תקנא בעשי עולה -- להיות כעושי עולה: the verse forbids emulating the wicked, not confronting them (= p_al_titchar_lihyot)
the whisperer's verse: 'do not compete with evil-doers, do not envy the unjust' (Ps 37:1)
ואומר: אל יקנא לבך בחטאים כי אם ביראת ה' כל היום (Prov 23:17) -- 'envy' in these verses is the wish to be like the sinners
שנאמר: יחילו דרכיו בכל עת (Ps 10:5) -- his ways prosper at all times
שנאמר: מרום משפטיך מנגדו (Ps 10:5) -- Your judgments are far beyond him
שנאמר: כל צורריו יפיח בהם (Ps 10:5) -- as for all his adversaries, he snorts at them

איני?! והאמר רבי יצחק: אם ראית רשע שהשעה משחקת לו אל תתגרה בו -- an amoraic memra forbids what R' Shimon ben Yochai permits (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind names an amoraic-memra contradiction)
R' Yitzchak: if you see a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, do not provoke him
דאמר רב הונא: מאי דכתיב... צדיק ממנו בולע, צדיק גמור אינו בולע -- the same distinction between the completely righteous and the not-completely righteous
ואיבעית אימא: הא והא ברשע שהשעה משחקת לו -- the permission is for a completely righteous provoker, the warning for one not completely righteous, דאמר רב הונא (= p_okimta_tzadik_gamur)
וכי רשע בולע צדיק? והא כתיב ה' לא יעזבנו בידו, וכתיב לא יאנה לצדיק כל און!
אלא: צדיק ממנו -- בולע, צדיק גמור -- אינו בולע (= p_tzadik_mimenu_bolea)
answer 3: both concern a wicked man on whom the hour smiles; the permission is for a completely righteous provoker, the warning for one not completely righteous
לא קשיא: הא במילי דידיה, הא במילי דשמיא -- the warning is for one's own affairs, the permission for matters of Heaven (= p_okimta_milei_dishmaya)
answer 1: R' Yitzchak's warning concerns one's own affairs; the permission concerns matters of Heaven
ואיבעית אימא: הא והא במילי דשמיא -- the warning is of a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, the permission of one on whom it does not (= p_okimta_shaah_mesachekat)
answer 2: both concern matters of Heaven; the warning is of a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, the permission of one on whom it does not
ואיבעית אימא: שעה משחקת לו -- שאני: the verse speaks of a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, and then it is different -- he swallows [even the righteous]
מזמור לדוד?! קינה לדוד מיבעי ליה! -- a man fleeing his own son should have composed a lament, not a psalm
David headed the psalm of his flight from Absalom 'a psalm (מזמור) of David' -- a psalm, not a lament
משל לאדם שיצא עליו שטר חוב... אף כן דוד: sad at the decree of evil from his house, glad once he saw it was Absalom, who would pity him -- משום הכי אמר מזמור (= p_samach_deavshalom)
so too David: when God told him 'I will raise up evil against you from your house' (II Sam 12:11) he was sad; once he saw that it was Absalom he was glad -- that is why he said 'a psalm'
the parable: a man against whom a promissory note was issued -- before he paid it he was sad, after he paid it he was glad
R' Elazar: the name Reuben -- Leah said: see the difference between my son and my father-in-law's son
and it is written: 'and he said, is he not rightly named Jacob, for he has supplanted me twice' (Gen 27:36)
whereas my son: Joseph took his birthright from him against his will -- 'and when he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph' (I Chr 5:1)
דאמר קרא: לכו חזו מפעלות ה' אשר שם שמות בארץ (Ps 46:9), אל תקרי שמות אלא שמות -- the names set upon the earth are the Lord's works, so a name shapes its bearer
a name is causative: the name given to a person shapes what befalls them -- the premise of the name-derashot, whose source the stam asks for
R' Yochanan: she is called Ruth because she merited that David, who inundated (ריוהו) the Holy One with songs and praises, issued from her
greater is the service of Torah than its study

שנאמר: מזמור לדוד בברחו מפני אבשלום בנו (Ps 3:1) וכתיב בתריה ה' מה רבו צרי רבים קמים עלי (Ps 3:2); ואילו גבי מלחמת גוג ומגוג כתיב למה רגשו גוים ולאמים יהגו ריק (Ps 2:1), ואילו מה רבו צרי לא כתיב -- an argument from the phrase's absence in the Gog-and-Magog psalm
a wayward household (bad offspring within a man's home) is harder for him than the war of Gog and Magog
Rav Nachman: I am not able [to come to the synagogue to pray]
